statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds at 20% at the bottom of the watch band as NQ eases to 30,834.75, deepening the overnight retracement to about 313 points, while Brent above 100 dollars, a 10-year near 5.29% and a Dow-versus-NQ split keep Stress at 76%.
recommendation: Tail is unchanged at 20% and remains five points below the 25% block threshold. The preceding assessment recorded a partial bounce to 30,878.25 inside the overnight fade; that bounce has given way and price has eased a further 44 points to 30,834.75, which deepens the retracement rather than reversing it. No Tail amplifier is observed. There is no session-extreme holding, no shallow-pullback sequence and no repeated extension after a failed retracement, and turnover has expanded to about 134k contracts while price fades, which is the signature of a functioning two-way book rather than of directional efficiency. The new development this hour is intra-equity dispersion: Dow futures are lower by roughly half a percent while NQ is higher by roughly half a percent and S&P 500 futures sit close to flat. Under the operative risk definition that split is a conflict, so it raises Stress to 76% and lowers directional conviction instead of raising Tail. The 12:00-15:00Z danger window covering jobless claims, Fed's Barkin, the cash open, the final manufacturing PMI and ISM manufacturing is unchanged and remains the hour range where observed post-release continuation would justify escalation.
headline: NQ eases to 30,834.75 as the overnight fade deepens to about 313 points, holding Tail at 20% while Dow futures diverge lower and Brent stays above 100 dollars
body: December E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures trade 30,834.75, up 136.00 points or 0.44% from the 30,698.75 settle, with a session range of 30,684.50 to 31,147.75 on about 134k contracts. Two independent sources corroborate the level at 30,850.75 and 30,836.25, so the price is well established across venues. The development of this hour is a renewed drift lower inside the existing fade. The previous assessment recorded 30,878.25 after roughly 270 points of the 449-point overnight advance had been retraced; price has since eased about 44 points, so the retracement has deepened to roughly 313 points and NQ now sits about 313 points below the 31,147.75 overnight high and about 260 points below the 31,094.75 pivot that earlier assessments named as the marker of genuine uptrend resumption. Turnover has expanded from about 125k to about 134k contracts while price fades, which is the opposite of the thin-volume drift that precedes a one-way path. A deepening retracement on expanding volume is ordinary two-way behaviour and is the structural opposite of the no-retracement path the Tail score is built to detect. The clearest new evidence is intra-equity dispersion. Nasdaq-100 futures are higher by roughly half a percent while Dow futures are lower by roughly half a percent and S&P 500 futures sit close to flat. That is rotation within the equity complex, not index-level one-way structure, and under the operative risk definition a conflict of that kind raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. Cross-asset conditions point the same way. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.29%, up about four basis points from a 5.26% prior close and rising for a fourth consecutive session, near its highest in roughly nineteen years; the Federal Reserve H.15 series corroborates the trend, with the 10-year moving from 5.11% on 23 September to 5.26% on 29 September while the 2-year ran 4.85% to 4.89%, so the curve continues to bear-steepen. Brent trades 100.26 dollars, up 2.28%, and WTI 91.83 dollars, up 1.56%, firming on an unresolved US-Iran impasse. Equities mixed while the long end sells off and crude holds above 100 dollars is a cross-asset conflict. VIX at 16.68, up 2.08% with a 16.32 to 17.00 range, is consistent with that reading: the move is higher but the absolute level remains low and gives no support to a pathological-path score. One scheduled item has printed since the previous assessment. September Challenger job cuts came in at 43,281 against a 52,881 prior and a consensus near 78.0K, the fewest announced cuts for any September since 2022 and a near 20% decline from a year earlier, with planned reductions down almost 40% across the first nine months of 2026. A labour market shedding fewer workers than expected is resilience evidence that sits naturally with the rising long end, and it is scored through Stress and Confidence rather than through Tail. The geopolitical backdrop has been verified against several reputable reports. Iran has received a US response to its proposal to revive the collapsed Gulf ceasefire, under which the United States would lift its blockade of Iranian ports and Iran would reopen the disrupted Strait of Hormuz within seven days, with the remaining disagreement over sequencing. That is an unresolved negotiation rather than a discontinuity, and its headline risk is two-sided: a sequencing agreement would be a crude-lower gap and a breakdown a crude-higher one. Two-sided headline risk of that character belongs in Stress. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and was not used as material evidence. Its collection timestamp is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly 35 hours old and far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, and its collection status is partial. Stale supporting context cannot establish current structure, so this assessment rests entirely on independent current research. The remainder of the day is dense. Initial and continuing jobless claims print at 12:30Z with consensus near 195K after a 197K prior, Fed's Barkin speaks at 13:05Z, the cash open is at 13:30Z, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI prints at 13:45Z and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z with ISM consensus a touch above the 54.6 prior. September non-farm payrolls, the unemployment rate and average hourly earnings follow tomorrow at 12:30Z, outside this forecast window. None of these scheduled items is treated as an automatic Tail escalation. The 7 August precedent is directly on point: a large payrolls surprise did not become a lethal no-retracement path, so event importance and dispersion are scored through Stress and Confidence until observed price action says otherwise. Confidence is 88%. Current NQ levels are corroborated across three sources, the 10-year is confirmed against both a live index and the Federal Reserve H.15 release, oil and VIX carry current quotes, the Challenger outcome is verified against two independent reports, the Gulf ceasefire state is verified across several reputable outlets, and the seven-day calendar is checked. The material gaps are the stale shared context file and the absence of a live 2-year quote, where the most recent authoritative value is the 29 September H.15 print; together these are a small completeness deduction against an otherwise current evidence set.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 15-16% through the European and early US hours of 30 September with the mode mixed, stepped into the watch band at 20% from 12:00Z as the US data block and the long-end selloff developed, and peaked at 23% around 15:00-16:00Z. It held 20-22% through the US afternoon and the early Asian session, then firmed steadily from 20% at 00:00Z through 21%, 22% and 23% to 24% at 05:00Z and 25% at 06:00Z as NQ printed successive fresh overnight highs and accepted above the 31,094.75 pivot, with the mode turning trend-up across those two slots. The 07:00Z slot returned to 22% and the mixed mode once the first liquid two-way test produced a 188-point retracement, and 08:00Z and 09:00Z held 20% as that retracement deepened past 300 points on expanding turnover. Stress rose steadily across the period from 66% to 75%, and Confidence held 85-88% throughout.
outlookSummary: The danger window is unchanged at 12:00-15:00Z, covering initial and continuing jobless claims at 12:30Z against consensus near 195K after 197K, Fed's Barkin at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z with ISM consensus near 54.7 against a 54.6 prior. Forecast Tail opens at 20% and holds there through the late-European hour where the deepest pre-US book normally extends rather than truncates a retracement, firms to 21% into the claims hour and 22% into Barkin and the cash open, and peaks at the top of the watch band at 24% across the 14:00Z ISM hour where Stress tops at 79%. It decays to 20-23% through the US afternoon, the 20:00Z cash close and the late evening, where Stress reaches its forecast-day low of 72%. It then firms through the Asian session and the European pre-open to 23-24% as positioning concentrates ahead of September non-farm payrolls at 12:30Z on 2 October, which falls outside this 24-hour window. The whole forecast path stays inside the watch band and no slot reaches the 25% block threshold, because scheduled event importance and dispersion are scored through Stress and Confidence rather than through Tail until an observed price path establishes mean-reversion failure. Confidence decays from 88% to 82% with forecast distance and recovers to 84% once European cash hours restore observable structure.
